page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula of orthoboric acid
lines: It is also called boric acid.
One molecule has one boron atom, three
hydrogen atoms and three oxygen atoms.
It is a white crystalline solid.
steps.why: The formula is the answer, and stating the atom count beside it settles the number of oxygen atoms, which is where this formula is most often written wrongly.
common_mistakes: Giving H₃BO₃ four oxygen atoms. It has three. Four oxygen atoms appear in the ion [B(OH)₄]⁻, which is a different species.
Writing HBO₂. That is metaboric acid, which forms when orthoboric acid is heated to 370 K.
steps.memory_tip: Read it straight off the formula: three H, one B, three O.
steps.margin_note: Write the name boric acid beside the formula. It costs one line.

steps.label: The same formula as B(OH)₃
steps.mark_note: The B(OH)₃ form or the nature of the acid
lines: The three hydrogen atoms sit on the
three oxygen atoms as OH groups, so
In water it is a weak monobasic Lewis
acid: it accepts OH⁻ instead of giving
up a proton of its own.
steps.why: Writing B(OH)₃ shows where the three hydrogen atoms actually sit, and that placement is what explains why the acid accepts OH⁻ from water rather than releasing H⁺.
common_mistakes: Reading H₃BO₃ as three hydrogen atoms bonded to boron. All three sit on oxygen, as OH groups.
Calling it tribasic because it has three hydrogen atoms. It is monobasic.
steps.memory_tip: Three OH groups on one boron is H₃BO₃ rewritten as B(OH)₃.
steps.margin_note: B(OH)₃ is an equally correct way to answer this question.

insider_note: The formula is four characters, so add the name boric acid and the B(OH)₃ form rather than stopping after one short line.
